provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the 1862 reads `Oratio T Eus` where the 1962 reads `Deus`; the 1862 reads `p6pulo` where the 1962 reads `populo` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1862 reads `me redmurincoelis PerDominum Secunda Oratio 8 Fclicis Presbyteri` where the 1962 reads `mereamur in caelis Per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum Filtum tuum Qui tecum vivit`; 5 further place(s) differ only in orthography, ligature or the recogniser's letterforms; the 1862 prints no conclusion at this place; the 1962 prints `Per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum Filtum tuum Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate`; the 1862 sets 14 point(s) of punctuation in this oration where the 1962 sets 9; the 1922 Mame reads `Ambrosium` where the 1962 reads `Hilarium`; the 1922 Mame reads `quem` where the 1962 reads `quern` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); 3 further place(s) differ only in orthography, ligature or the recogniser's letterforms; the 1922 Mame abbreviates the conclusion to `Per Dominum Et in Missis` where the 1962 writes it out as `Per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum Filtum tuum Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate`. Corroboration: 1922 Tours Mame, printed p. 490 (artifact PDF p. 604), target-body character coverage 0.95, found by whole-book sweep (bounding-box reflow); Benziger 1962 conformed printing, target-body character coverage 0.87.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui populo tuo aeternae salutis beatum Hilarium ministrum tribuisti:
praesta, quaesumus; ut, quem Doctorem vitae habuimus in terris,
intercessorem habere mereamur in caelis. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum,
Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

translations.caution: Original study translation; not approved for liturgical use or recitation.
translations.text: God, you gave blessed Hilary to your people as a minister of eternal salvation. Grant, we ask, that we may be found worthy to have as our intercessor in heaven the one we had as a teacher of life on earth. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.

ordinary_disposition.basis: Printed after the Postcommunions as an alternative Epistle for Doctors.

taken_from.citation: Missa In medio, de Communi Doctorum [22]

provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. The 1962 wording was read on 2026-10-01 on that edition's page image at 200 and again at 400 dpi (printed p. 442, no. 1917, marked C I; artifact PDF p. 523, right column, under 'Die 14 ianuarii, S. Hilarii Ep., Conf. et Eccl. Doct.'), not on any text layer, and the string the 2026-09-04 backfill had stored and quarantined for recogniser damage was not used. Every word was then read on the 1922 Tours Mame at printed p. 26* (artifact PDF p. 904), Commune Doctorum, Pro Doctore Pontifice, Secreta, read on its page image at 300 dpi, which carries the text word for word. Differences from the antecedent: the Mame prints the Common's rubrical blank N. where the 1962 writes the day's saint, Hilarii, into it: filling a rubrical blank; the Mame sets a comma after Doctoris and after quae; the Mame prints the short conclusion cue Per Dominum where the 1962 writes it out. Full collation, replacing the eleven-word truncated target of the earlier lane. The antecedents that lane recorded do not carry these words: the 1862's own Hilary Secret (text-layer lines 55176-55181) reads Sancti tui Hilarii nobis, without Pontificis ... atque Doctoris, and its 7 March formula reads Confessoris where the 1962 reads Pontificis, each a different word. The 1922 Mame's Commune Doctorum, read on its page image at printed p. 26* (artifact PDF p. 904), prints this Secret pro Doctore Pontifice word for word with N. in the name slot.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Sancti Hilarii Pontificis tui atque Doctoris nobis, Domine, pia non desit
oratio: quae et munera nostra conciliet; et tuam nobis indulgentiam semper
obtineat. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit
et regnat in unitate.

translations.caution: Original study translation; not approved for liturgical use or recitation.
translations.text: Lord, may the devout prayer of Saint Hilary, your Bishop and Doctor, never fail us; may it win acceptance for our gifts and always obtain your forgiveness for us. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Ut nobis, Domine, tua sacrificia dent salutem: beatus Hilarius
Pontifex tuus et Doctor egregius, quaesumus, precator accedat. Per
Dominum nostrum.

translations.caution: Original study translation; not approved for liturgical use or recitation.
translations.text: So that your sacrifices may bring us salvation, Lord, we ask that blessed Hilary, your Bishop and a distinguished Doctor, may come forward to intercede. Through our Lord.
